text:
Predicates:
BreedingBack(x) ::: x is a form of breeding back.
ArtificialSelection(x) ::: x is a form of artificial selection.
SelectiveBreeding(x) ::: x is a form of selective breeding.
DomesticAnimal(x) ::: x is a domestic animal.
HeckCattle(x) ::: x is a Heck cattle.
Aurochs(x) ::: x is an aurochs.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Extinct(x) ::: x is extinct.
Resemble(x, y) ::: x resembles y.
Premises:
BreedingBack(breedingBack) ∧ ArtificialSelection(breedingBack) ∧ SelectiveBreeding(breedingBack) ∧ ∀x (BreedingBack(x) → ∃y (DomesticAnimal(y) ∧ SelectiveBreeding(x, y))) ::: Breeding back is a form of artificial selection by the deliberate selective breeding of domestic animals.
∃x (HeckCattle(x) ∧ ∃y (Aurochs(y) ∧ Resemble(x, y))) ::: Heck cattle were bred-back in the 1920s to resemble the aurochs.
Animal(heckCattle) ::: Heck cattle are animals.
Animal(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are animals.
∃x ∃y (Animal(x) ∧ Animal(y) ∧ Extinct(y) ∧ Resemble(x, y)) ::: Some animals to be bred-back resemble animals that are extinct.
Conclusion:
Extinct(aurochs) ::: Aurochs are extinct.
